steps.note: In Notes, add a note to the Introduction saying why a rise at a gauge does not say which ground would flood, with the vertical-datum diagram from this repository.

steps.label: The note
steps.value: A projected rise is a change in the sea’s level at a tide gauge. Saying which ground it would reach needs the height of the ground and the height of the local sea measured from the same surface, and open terrain models measure from a geoid, not from the local sea.

steps.label: Picture: PNG, JPEG, WebP or SVG
Alt text: what the picture shows
steps.value: A cross-section of a low coast, not to scale. From the bottom: the WGS84 ellipsoid; the geoid; local mean sea level over 1995–2014, the AR6 baseline, above the geoid by an offset; and a projected sea level above that. On land, bare ground and the surface with roofs and trees.

steps.label: Caption: what a reader is to take from it
steps.value: Heights and the surfaces they are measured from. A terrain model gives H above the geoid; a projection is a rise above local mean sea level; comparing them needs the offset between the two. Not to scale.

steps.note: Then the write-up as it would be submitted: what was asked, the sources and methods, what was found, and what it does not say. Each work is cited through the note’s citation builder and numbered in References.

steps.label: The note
steps.value: Health facilities on low coasts are among the services a rising sea reaches first, and planning for them starts from a projection that applies to the place. IPCC AR6 publishes projections of relative sea-level change at tide gauges and on a grid, for several emissions scenarios. We asked which published projection applies to each of 194 health facilities in coastal Manila, how far from the facility it is measured, and how much sea level is projected to rise there by 2100.

steps.label: The work names more authors than these (et al.)
Title
steps.value: Ocean, Cryosphere and Sea Level Change

steps.label: Journal or containing work
steps.value: Climate Change 2021: The Physical Science Basis. Contribution of Working Group I to the Sixth Assessment Report of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change

steps.label: The note
steps.value: **Projections.** IPCC AR6 Sea Level Projections, version 20210809, medium confidence, extracted for the eight Philippine sites that are tide gauges: 288 values, for SSP1-2.6, SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5, with and without vertical land motion, for 2050 and 2100, at the 0.17, 0.5 and 0.83 levels, in millimetres above the 1995–2014 mean. The middle level is reported as the median and the outer two as the likely range.

steps.label: The work names more authors than these (et al.)
Title
steps.value: IPCC AR6 Sea Level Projections, version 20210809

steps.label: The work names more authors than these (et al.)
Title
steps.value: The Framework for Assessing Changes To Sea-level (FACTS) v1.0

steps.label: The note
steps.value: **Facilities.** 194 named hospitals (17) and clinics (177) from OpenStreetMap, found with Find health facilities in the Humanitarian OpenStreetMap Team’s Philippines export (rebuilt 2026-05-05) and kept where they fall in a box over coastal Manila, 120.93° to 121.05° E and 14.52° to 14.68° N. © OpenStreetMap contributors, Open Database License 1.0. OpenStreetMap states no completeness, so this is what is mapped, not a register.

steps.label: The note
steps.value: **Nearest gauge and its projection.** Each facility’s nearest gauge, and the great-circle distance to it on a sphere of 6,371.0088 km, came from Measure distance. Select rows narrowed the projections to one scenario, SSP2-4.5; one family, with vertical land motion; one year, 2100; and the median. Relate then brought that value beside each facility, matching its nearest gauge to the projections’ site.

steps.label: The note
steps.value: **Why these choices.** SSP2-4.5 is an intermediate scenario, not a forecast. The family with vertical land motion is the change relative to the land, which is the change a building on that land meets; the family without it is reported beside it to show how much of the change is the land’s own motion. The median is reported with its likely range.

steps.label: The note
steps.value: All 194 facilities are nearest the Manila, South Harbor gauge, PSMSL 145, at 0.9 to 13.4 km; the median distance is 6.5 km, and 61 are within 5 km.

steps.label: The note
steps.value: By 2100 under SSP2-4.5, relative sea level at the Manila gauge is projected to rise 1,124 mm above the 1995–2014 mean (likely range 963 to 1,366 mm), including vertical land motion. Without it, the same projection is 602 mm (442 to 841 mm), so the land’s motion accounts for about 520 mm of the median.

steps.label: The note
steps.value: The land’s own motion roughly doubles the projected rise at Manila. The tide gauge’s record at PSMSL notes a rising trend “suspected to be due to deposition from the river discharges and excessive reclamation although subsidence not totally discarded”. A projection that left out vertical land motion would understate the change facilities here meet.

steps.label: Authors, one per line
steps.value: Permanent Service for Mean Sea Level

steps.label: The note
steps.value: **Not a flood map.** A rise at a gauge does not say which ground it would reach: that needs the ground’s height and the local sea’s, measured from the same surface. At the Manila gauge, EGM2008, which DeltaDTM and other open terrain models measure from, and NAMRIA’s gravimetric geoid agree within 2 mm (43.009 and 43.011 m above the ellipsoid), and NAMRIA’s geoid fitted to mean sea level stands 0.85 m above both, within about 10 cm. Which years that mean sea level stands for is not stated by NAMRIA, and it matters: the gauge’s 1995–2014 mean, the AR6 baseline, stands 104 to 757 mm above the means of earlier 19-year periods. No facility is said to lie below a projected sea level.

steps.value: A new Philippine geoid model from airborne and terrestrial gravity data

steps.label: The note
steps.value: **One projection for all.** Every facility takes the Manila gauge’s projection, from 0.9 to 13.4 km away. A projection is for its gauge, and how much the change varies across the city is not known from these data. The facilities are what OpenStreetMap maps, and an absence among them is not an absence on the ground.

steps.label: The note
steps.value: **Checks.** The eight AR6 site numbers were compared with PSMSL’s station pages: number, name and position agree for all eight, although AR6’s own pages do not state the numbering. Both workflows were built by performing this repository’s manual from an empty canvas, and the published project is the result of that run.
